chapter_theme: A song at Koodalaiyatrur (திருக்கூடலையாற்றூர்): the poet confesses that deeds, the three desires and women's charms brought disease, and asks that when Death's summons comes Kalan not approach; the praise names Siva at Madurai bearing sand, the goddess who burned Death, and Murugan who lives in the poet's heart.

756.reading: The poet says that his deeds surrounded him, desire and the three desires lit a fire like an axe heated in the forge, and that, adorned with flowers, sandal, civet and rosewater, he sported with women of painted eyes until caught in their net, then disease, pain and wind came on him, and he had no love for Murugan; he asks that when Yama's men drive him and the summons marked by Brahma arrives, cruel Kalan not come near, and that Murugan give him his grace and love. The praise names Murugan who freed the gods with the vel and loved the hunter girl, Siva who came to Madurai in another form and bore sand on the Vaigai's bank, burned the cities and rides the bull, the goddess who burned Death, and Murugan who leapt so that Death fell and who lives in the poet's body, at the meeting of the Vellar and Manimuthar.
756.nuance: மூவாசை are the three desires, for land, gold and women by tradition. சீட்டு is Death's written summons, which Brahma has marked (வேதன் அடையாளம்). The praise turns the same motif round: கூற்றுவனைக் காய்ந்த அபிராமி and கூற்று விழத் தாண்டி name the goddess and Murugan as conquerors of Death. மதுராபுரியில் ஆடி வைகை ஆற்றின் மணல் தாங்கு is Siva's carrying earth at Madurai, and எனது ஆகமதில் வாழ் places Murugan within the poet.

links.note: Both set the Lord against Death's servants at the hour of death; Tirumular says they will not harm those who think of the Lord, 756 confesses a life without that love and asks Murugan to keep Kalan away.
